issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 16/07/26

✅ Implementation: Profile Published Folder Bookmarks API

Example API

Endpoint: GET /bookmark/published/profile/:username
Description: Retrieves paginated published bookmark folders for a profile user. This endpoint powers the published bookmark folder list in profile.

Example cURL Request

curl -G "http://localhost:3000/bookmark/published/profile/<username>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" \
  -H "role: viewer" \
  -H "ec: false" \
  --data-urlencode "page=1" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=9"

Request Parameters

  • username (string, required): Profile username.
  • page (int, optional): Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1.
  • limit (int, optional): Number of folders per page. Defaults to 9.

Headers

  • Authorization (string, required): Bearer token.
  • role (string, required): Allowed values are viewer, user, and my-user.
  • ec (string, optional): Set true for encrypted response. Defaults to plain JSON behavior.

Role Rules

  • viewer: can list public published bookmark folders for a profile.
  • user: can list another user's public published bookmark folders, with blocked/deactive checks.
  • my-user: can list only the authenticated user's own profile. If :username belongs to another user, returns 403.
  • Other roles return 401 Unauthorized.

Data Source

This endpoint reads from:

public.views_published_folders

It also joins:

public.folder_bookmark

The join is used to make published_at reliable:

COALESCE(v.published_at, fb.published_at, fb.updated_at, fb.created_at) AS published_at

Success Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "messages": "List Published Folder Bookmark Profile",
    "folders": [
      {
        "slug": "ob97a4a99d3-2026040810361400",
        "name": "CN Tower",
        "thumbnail": "thumbnail.jpg",
        "published_at": "2026-07-16T00:00:00Z",
        "total_bookmark": 12
      }
    ],
    "total": 24,
    "page": 1,
    "limit": 9
  }
}

Empty Response

If the profile exists but has no published folders, the endpoint returns an empty list.

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "messages": "List Published Folder Bookmark Profile",
    "folders": [],
    "total": 0,
    "page": 1,
    "limit": 9
  }
}

User Not Found Response

{
  "statusCode": 409,
  "data": {
    "status": "Conflict",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "User Not Found"
    }
  }
}

Forbidden Response

Returned when role: my-user is used for another user's profile, or when a user has blocked the target profile.

{
  "statusCode": 403,
  "data": {
    "status": "Forbidden",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "This is not your profile"
    }
  }
}

Unauthorized Response

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "data": {
    "status": "Unauthorized",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Unauthorized"
    }
  }
}

Summary

Implemented a profile API that lists published bookmark folders for a target user. The endpoint uses the existing published folder view and returns a minimal folder response for the profile bookmark tab.

Endpoint

GET /bookmark/published/profile/:username?page=1&limit=9

Files Changed

  • src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/ListPublishedFolderBookmarkProfile.go
  • src/Controllers/V1/BookmarksControllers.go
  • src/Routes/V1/BookmarksRoutes.go
  • src/Models/FolderBookmarkModel.go
  • api-collection/Panorra API Feeds/Posts/Folder Bookmark/List Published Folder Bookmark Profile.yml

Response Fields

Each folder item returns:

  • slug
  • name
  • thumbnail
  • published_at
  • total_bookmark

No created_at field is returned.

Role Handling

Supported roles:

  • viewer
  • user
  • my-user

Unsupported roles return 401 Unauthorized.

For viewer, the API returns published public folder data from views_published_folders.

For user, the API validates authenticated user data, rejects a blocked target profile, and filters deactive target users.

For my-user, the API requires the target user id to match c.Locals("userId"). This prevents role: my-user from reading another username's profile and avoids unnecessary blocked/deactive checks for the user's own profile.

Query

The endpoint uses views_published_folders and joins folder_bookmark to make published_at reliable:

SELECT
  v.slug,
  v.name,
  v.thumbnail,
  COALESCE(v.published_at, fb.published_at, fb.updated_at, fb.created_at) AS published_at,
  v.total_bookmark
FROM views_published_folders AS v
LEFT JOIN folder_bookmark AS fb ON fb.slug = v.slug
WHERE v.owner_username = ?
ORDER BY COALESCE(v.published_at, fb.published_at, fb.updated_at, fb.created_at) DESC
LIMIT ?
OFFSET ?

Pagination

Defaults:

  • page = 1
  • limit = 9

Response includes:

  • total
  • page
  • limit

Added:

api-collection/Panorra API Feeds/Posts/Folder Bookmark/List Published Folder Bookmark Profile.yml

Includes:

  • default request
  • 200 response example
  • 409 User Not Found response example

issues.display_title: Issue #468: Published Folder Bookmark Detail API
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 16/07/26

✅ Implementation: Published Folder Bookmark Header API

Example API

Endpoint: GET /bookmark/published/:slug
Description: Retrieves one published bookmark folder by exact slug. This endpoint is used for the folder detail/header data, so the frontend can refresh /bookmark/published/:slug without relying on search results.

Example cURL Request

curl -G "http://localhost:3000/bookmark/published/<slug>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" \
  -H "ec: false"

Request Parameters

  • slug (string, required): Published folder bookmark slug.

Visibility Rules

  • Role viewer can access public published folder detail.
  • Role user can access public published folder detail.
  • Other roles return 401 Unauthorized.
  • All roles exclude deactivated owners.
  • Role user also excludes blocked owners.

Data Source

This endpoint reads from:

public.views_published_folders

Required view columns:

  • id
  • slug
  • name
  • description
  • location
  • location_name
  • category_name
  • published_at
  • total_bookmark
  • thumbnail
  • owner_username
  • owner_fullname
  • owner_avatar
  • owner_encrypt

It also checks:

public.broadcast

The broadcast check is used to set potd.

Success Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "messages": "Published Folder Bookmark",
    "bookmark": {
      "slug": "cn-tower",
      "name": "CN Tower",
      "description": "Published folder description",
      "location": {
        "lat": 43.6426,
        "lng": -79.3871
      },
      "location_name": "Toronto",
      "category_name": "Leisure",
      "published_at": "2026-07-16T00:00:00Z",
      "potd": false,
      "total_bookmark": {
        "counter_bookmak": 12
      },
      "thumbnail": "thumbnail.jpg",
      "user": {
        "username": "sunnybreeze",
        "fullname": "Sunny Breeze",
        "avatar": "avatar.jpg",
        "encrypt": "abcd123"
      }
    }
  }
}

Not Found Response

If the folder slug does not exist or is hidden by deactivated/blocked owner filtering:

  "statusCode": 409,
  "data": {
    "status": "Conflict",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Folder Not Found"
    }
  }
}

Unauthorized Response

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "data": {
    "status": "Unauthorized",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Unauthorized"
    }
  }
}

FE Usage Example

Use this endpoint for folder detail/header data:

curl -G "http://localhost:3000/bookmark/published/<slug>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" \
  -H "ec: false"

Then load posts from:

curl -G "http://localhost:3000/bookmark/published/<slug>/posts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" \
  -H "ec: false" \
  --data-urlencode "page=1" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=10"

Summary

Implemented a dedicated published folder detail endpoint so FE can load or refresh a folder detail page directly by slug. This replaces the previous dependency on /search/folder-bookmark/published search results for detail data.

Endpoint

GET /bookmark/published/:slug

Files Changed

  • src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/PublishedFolderBookmark.go
  • src/Controllers/V1/BookmarksControllers.go
  • src/Routes/V1/BookmarksRoutes.go
  • src/Routes/V1/BookmarksRoutes_test.go
  • api-collection/Panorra API Feeds/Posts/Folder Bookmark/Published Folder Bookmark Header.yml

Implementation Details

Action

Created PublishedFolderBookmark in src/Action/V1/Bookmarks.

Behavior:

  • Reads slug from route params.
  • Supports role viewer and user.
  • Rejects unsupported roles with 401 Unauthorized.
  • Loads deactive users from Redis key:
    • <prefix>_deactive_users_ec
  • For role user, loads:
    • user data through UserFunctions.UserDatas
    • blocked users from <prefix>_blocked_users_ec_<encrypt>
  • Queries views_published_folders by exact slug.

Core query:

query := Config.DB.Table("views_published_folders").
    Select("id, slug, name, description, location, location_name, category_name, published_at, total_bookmark, thumbnail, owner_username, owner_fullname, owner_avatar, owner_encrypt").
    Where("slug = ?", slug)

Blocked/deactivated owner filter:

if len(notInEncrypt) > 0 {
    query = query.Where("owner_encrypt NOT IN (?)", notInEncrypt)
}

If the query does not find a visible folder, the endpoint returns:

409 Folder Not Found

Response Mapping

The response reuses Models.SearchFolderBookmark so the detail payload stays compatible with search result folder items.

Mapped fields:

  • user object from owner columns:
    • owner_username
    • owner_fullname
    • owner_avatar
    • owner_encrypt
  • total_bookmark object:
    • counter_bookmak
  • potd flag by checking broadcast.folder_id = folderBookmark.ID

The counter_bookmak typo is preserved for existing FE compatibility.

Goal

Create a dedicated detail endpoint for a published bookmark folder so the frontend can open or refresh /bookmark/published/:slug without depending on search results.

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 31/07/26

✅ Implementation: Add Onboarding Details to User Detail Response

Overview

This document outlines the implementation for PR #472: Add onboarding details to User Detail response.

The change updates the GET /users/detail response so the client receives onboarding state alongside the existing user detail payload.

Commits

  • 2a37a043 - Add onboarding details to User Detail response
  • 6533b008 - Enhance User Detail response to include onboarding information and user ID
  • c27e9cf1 - Merge pull request #472 from feat/471-onboarding-user-detail

Files Modified

  1. src/Action/V1/Users/UserDetail.go
  2. src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions/UsersFunctions.go
  3. api-collection/Panorra API Feeds/User/User Detail.yml
  4. go.mod

Implementation Details

1. User Detail Action

Updated src/Action/V1/Users/UserDetail.go in the non-v=0 response path.

The Action now:

  • Loads the current user data using UserFunctions.UserDatas(c, encrypt, "detail").
  • Uses userData["user_id"] to query onboarding data from user_detail.
  • Adds the onboarding payload to the response as res["onboarding"].
  • Removes user_id from the returned user detail result before sending the response.

Onboarding query:

qOnboarding := Config.DB.Table("user_detail").
    Select("onboarding_completed, discovery_source, place_interests, usage_intent, onboarding_completed_at").
    Where("user_id = ?", userData["user_id"]).
    Scan(&onboarding)

If the onboarding query fails, the endpoint returns 500 Internal Server Error.

2. place_interests JSON Parsing

place_interests is stored as a JSON string. The Action parses it into []string before returning it.

if raw, ok := onboarding["place_interests"].(string); ok && raw != "" {
    var interests []string
    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &interests); err != nil {
        return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 500, fiber.ErrInternalServerError.Message, "Internal Server Error")
    }
    onboarding["place_interests"] = interests
}

This changes the API response from a raw JSON string to a native JSON array.

3. User Helper Update

Updated src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions/UsersFunctions.go.

For UserDatas(c, encrypt, "detail"), the helper now includes:

response["user_id"] = userDetail["id"]

This lets UserDetail query user_detail by user_id without joining through users.encrypt.

The Action deletes user_id before returning the public response.

4. API Collection Update

Updated api-collection/Panorra API Feeds/User/User Detail.yml example response to include:

"onboarding": {
  "onboarding_completed": false,
  "discovery_source": "social_media",
  "place_interests": ["attractions", "nature_scenery"],
  "usage_intent": null,
  "onboarding_completed_at": null
}

Response Shape

GET /users/detail

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "messages": "User Detail",
    "onboarding": {
      "onboarding_completed": false,
      "discovery_source": "social_media",
      "place_interests": ["attractions", "nature_scenery"],
      "usage_intent": null,
      "onboarding_completed_at": null
    },
    "result": {
      "avatar": "",
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "encrypt": "ecxxxx",
      "fullname": "Example User",
      "username": "example"
    }
  }
}

Notes

  • The onboarding payload is added only to the current non-v=0 User Detail response path.
  • include filtering still applies only to result; onboarding remains a separate response object.
  • user_id is used internally for the onboarding lookup and removed from the response.

Verification

Ran:

go test ./...

Result: pass.

Read side of the Personalization Onboarding flow specified in panorra-pwa#3223 (formerly named "KYC").

The frontend needs this to redirect users who already completed the flow (§14 "Completed users should be redirected away from onboarding") and to restore selections after a browser refresh (§14 "Saved selections should persist after refresh").

Related

  • Blocked by the migration — GoThruMedia/panorra-api-new#417. The columns must exist before this ships.
  • Write side — GoThruMedia/panorra-api-new#416

No new endpoint

GET /users/detail already exists (src/Routes/V1/UsersRoutes.go:11) and is what the PWA calls. It just needs to carry five more columns.

The change goes in the else branch, not the v=0 branch

This is the part that is easy to get wrong.

The PWA calls GET /users/detail?pw=true (auth.service.ts:132) — no v=0. That lands in the else branch at src/Action/V1/Users/UserDetail.go:81, which reads from UserFunctions.UserDatas(c, encrypt, "detail").

That helper returns only avatar, email, encrypt, fullname and username out of the Redis cache. It never touches the user_detail table at all. Adding columns to the Select on line 47 — the v=0 branch — would compile, pass a manual Bruno test against ?v=0, and still ship nothing the PWA can see.

Add after the userData["status"] == "error" guard:

		var onboarding map[string]interface{}
		Config.DB.Table("user_detail as ud").
			Joins("JOIN users as u ON u.id = ud.user_id").
			Select("ud.onboarding_completed, ud.discovery_source, ud.place_interests, ud.usage_intent, ud.onboarding_completed_at").
			Where("u.encrypt = ?", encrypt).
			Scan(&onboarding)
		res["onboarding"] = onboarding

Place res["onboarding"] outside the if include != "" block. Inside it, a request carrying ?include= would strip the field and the frontend would fail to detect completed users.

Also add the five columns to the Select in the v=0 branch (line 47) so both paths agree.

No Redis invalidation needed

ReplaceUserDetails caches only users.* plus last_login (src/Utils/Redis/Redis.go:233-235) and never touches the preference columns. The query above hits the database directly, so a write from POST /users/onboarding in the other repo is visible immediately — no cache busting required.

Response shape

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "User Detail",
    "result": { "...": "existing fields unchanged" },
    "onboarding": {
      "onboarding_completed": false,
      "discovery_source": "social_media",
      "place_interests": ["attractions", "nature_scenery"],
      "usage_intent": null,
      "onboarding_completed_at": null
    }
  }
}

A user who has never started the flow gets onboarding_completed: false with the other four fields null.

Acceptance criteria

  • GET /users/detail?pw=true returns the onboarding object
  • The field survives a request that also passes ?include=
  • GET /users/detail?v=0 returns the same five columns
  • A user who never started the flow returns onboarding_completed: false and nulls, not an error
  • Existing response fields are unchanged — this is additive only
  • Bruno collection updated

Out of scope

Saving the answers is the write side, in the other repo — see panorra-api-new#416. This task is read-only.

QA Summary — 21 August 2026

Verdict: PASSED — the onboarding object is correctly present in the default response path, survives ?include= filtering, persists through encrypted response, and user_id is not leaked to the public response. No coding bugs found.

Note on ?v=0 branch: The onboarding object is absent from the GET /users/detail?v=0 response. This is an intentional scoping decision documented in the RESULT section: "The onboarding payload is added only to the current non-v=0 User Detail response path." issues.display_title: Issue #463: Implement User Interest Collection System (Tags/Categories)
issues.main_description_html:
Description

To personalize the user experience on the platform, we need a system to track what content categories or tags each user is interested in. This will allow us to serve relevant content (e.g., mapping users to tags like "360 panoramas", "virtual tours", "AI editing", or "equirectangular landscapes").

Now that we collect user interests (tags/categories), we need to utilize this data to serve personalized content on the platform. The main data feed (e.g., panoramas, projects, or posts) should prioritize items that match the user's saved interests.

Row Specifications

Row 1 — "Recommended for You" (main post shelf)

Purpose: Core interest-ranked post feed. Expandable to full infinite scroll via "See more."

Scoring formula:

score = (0.30 × interest_match_score)
      + (0.20 × engagement_velocity)
      + (0.15 × like_rate)
      + (0.10 × view_completion_rate)
      + (0.10 × save_rate)
      + (0.10 × share_rate)
      + (0.05 × recency_decay)
      − (0.15 × repetition_penalty)
Criteria Definition Rationale
interest_match_score Cosine similarity between user interest vector and post category tags Core personalization signal — highest weight
engagement_velocity (likes + comments + saves) / hours_since_post, normalized Surfaces rising content early, not just all-time popular
like_rate likes / impressions Direct, cheap positive signal
view_completion_rate % of sphere explored (pan_degrees / 360) weighted with dwell time vs. median 360-specific: confirms real engagement, not a glance
save_rate saves / impressions Stronger intent than a like
share_rate shares / impressions Strongest signal but sparse — lower weight due to volume, not value
recency_decay Exponential decay, half-life ~48–72 hrs Keeps feed fresh without killing older quality content
repetition_penalty Penalty if same creator/category appeared in last N items Prevents monotony

Qualifying thresholds:

  • Minimum resolution_score to filter broken/low-quality uploads
  • Minimum impression count before engagement_velocity is trusted (avoid overfitting to early likes)
    Refresh cadence: Re-ranked every 5–10 min (cached); full recompute nightly

Row 2 — "Creators You Might Like" (user suggestions)

Purpose: Suggest accounts to follow based on interest overlap and social proof.

Scoring formula:

score = (0.35 × category_overlap_score)
      + (0.20 × creator_quality_score)
      + (0.15 × mutual_follow_signal)
      + (0.15 × recent_activity_score)
      + (0.10 × follower_growth_rate)
      − (0.05 × already_seen_penalty)
Criteria Definition Rationale
category_overlap_score % of creator's posts matching user's top 3 interest categories Core relevance signal
creator_quality_score avg(resolution_score) across creator's recent posts Avoid prolific-but-low-quality accounts
mutual_follow_signal # of accounts the user follows who also follow this creator Social proof
recent_activity_score Days since last post, decayed Avoid suggesting inactive accounts
follower_growth_rate % follower growth, trailing 30 days Surfaces rising creators, not just biggest accounts
already_seen_penalty Suppress if shown in last N sessions with no follow action Avoid suggestion fatigue

Exclusion rules: Never suggest already-followed, blocked, or muted users
Refresh cadence: Daily batch recompute

Row 3 — "Trending in [Category]" (rotating category shelf)

Purpose: Surface hot content within the user's top interest category.

Category selection:

selected_category = argmax(user_interest_score × category_content_availability)

Picks the user's top interest category that also has sufficient fresh content volume.

Post ranking within row:

score = (0.40 × engagement_velocity_within_category)
      + (0.25 × recency_decay)
      + (0.20 × like_rate)
      + (0.15 × view_completion_rate)

Note: no interest_match_score here — category is already fixed; this row answers "what's hot right now" within a liked category.

Refresh cadence: Category selection re-evaluated daily; posts refreshed every 15–30 min

Row 4 — "Popular Hashtags for You"

Purpose: Surface relevant, emerging hashtags to deepen category exploration.

Scoring formula:

score = (0.35 × user_category_affinity)
      + (0.30 × hashtag_growth_rate)
      + (0.20 × post_count_in_hashtag)
      + (0.15 × avg_engagement_per_post_in_hashtag)
Criteria Definition Rationale
user_category_affinity Overlap between hashtag's dominant category and user's interest profile Relevance
hashtag_growth_rate % increase in posts/day, trailing 7 days Surfaces emerging trends, not just evergreen tags
post_count_in_hashtag Total posts (log-scaled) Avoid near-empty hashtags
avg_engagement_per_post Mean(likes+saves) per post in hashtag Quality signal

Refresh cadence: Daily

Row 5 — "New Places to Explore" (serendipity / anti-filter-bubble)

Purpose: Deliberately surface content outside the user's established interest pattern to preserve the platform's "explore the world" value prop.

Scoring formula:

score = (0.30 × geo_novelty_score)
      + (0.25 × category_adjacency_score)
      + (0.20 × global_quality_score)
      + (0.15 × engagement_velocity)
      + (0.10 × diversity_bonus)
Criteria Definition Rationale
geo_novelty_score Inverse of user's historical engagement with a region (higher = less seen) Surfaces unfamiliar geography
category_adjacency_score Similarity to user's interests but not identical (e.g. nature → adventure/underwater, not more nature) Adjacent discovery, not random noise
global_quality_score Blend of resolution_score + engagement_velocity, category-agnostic Ensures serendipity picks remain good content
engagement_velocity Same as Row 1 Avoid surfacing dead content just because it's novel
diversity_bonus Bonus if creator/region hasn't appeared elsewhere on page Reinforces row's distinct purpose

Constraint: Capped at ~10% of total page real estate — job is exposure, not depth
Refresh cadence: Daily

Sub-tasks

Summary

Scope

Profile Query

The handler queries the authenticated user's profile fields:

    CoverImage *string
    Website    *string
}

    Select("cover_image, website").

Both fields are pointers so database NULL values remain JSON null.

Social Links Query

Added a response-only type:

    Type string `json:"type"`
    URL  string `json:"url"`
}

Links are queried by authenticated user ID:

Config.DB.Table("user_social_links").
    Select("type, url").
    Where("user_id = ?", userData["user_id"]).
    Order("position ASC").
    Scan(&socialLinks)

Initializing the slice with []userSocialLinkResponse{} ensures users without links receive [] instead of null.

Response Assignment

Fields are assigned directly:

userData["cover_image"] = profile.CoverImage
userData["website"] = profile.Website
